title.narrative: Enhancing Public-Private Partnerships In Punjab Project

description.narrative: The project will provide financing for the project development facility (PDF) to support line departments in engaging the assistance of experienced transaction advisors. The ADB loan will be used to fund a dedicated viability gap fund (VGF) window that will be managed by the Planning and Development Department (PDD). The project is aligned with the following impact: private sector investments and overall employment in Punjab increased. The project will have the following outcome: sustainable and fiscally responsible public-private partnership (PPP) projects that offer value for money (VFM) increased. The outputs are (i) PDF and VGF resources for PPP projects augmented, and (ii) PPP institutional capacity enhanced and strengthened.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: PDF and VGF resources for PPP projects augmented. Indicator: Twelve PPP project proposals with PDF support submitted and reviewed by the RMU and the PPPC by 2025, with at least one social project approved with direct benefits to vulnerable groups such as the poor, women, girls, elderly, and persons with disabilities (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: An amount of $0.833 million (equivalent PKR 129 million) has been disbursed and utilized for preparation of 14 PDF projects, primarily relating to infrastructure and road sectors.
Loan closed on 30 June 2025 without any progress on this project. Data Source: PPPPA reports; ADB review mission reports; updates as disclosed in P&DD website Actual value:

Output: PPP institutional capacity enhanced and strengthened. Indicator: At least three locally-held PPP Investment Conferences delivered to increase awareness from prospective private investors by 2022. (2017 Baseline: No local conference held in Punjab) Progress/Status: 3 PPP investment conferences were executed for the priority Water Meters and Multan Vehari Road subprojects. Data Source: Investment conference reports and coverage Actual value:

Output: PDF and VGF resources for PPP projects augmented. Indicator: Two PPP projects awarded with VGF support by 2025 (2017 baseline: 1) Progress/Status: Contract award and advance disbursement of VGF for water meters subproject was completed.
The second priority project- Multan-Vehari Road was no longer pursued under PPP mode due to government decision to proceed with conventional procurement using government funds.
Loan closed on 30 June 2025 without any progress on this project. Data Source: PPPPA reports; ADB review mission reports; updates as disclosed in P&DD website Actual value:

Output: PPP institutional capacity enhanced and strengthened. Indicator: At least three PPP training programs delivered to relevant government agencies, with women accounting for 20% of participants from at least one department, by 2025. (2017 Baseline: No PPP training arrangements in place) Progress/Status: APMG, gender safeguards and procurement trainings were undertaken in Q4 2021 and Q1 2022. Gender safeguards training in Dec 2021 had 40% women participation. APMG training in Jan 2022 had 42% women participation from PPPPA. Data Source: Training calendar and reports. Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y

Output: PPP institutional capacity enhanced and strengthened. Indicator: ESMS, with social and gender indicators, established and adopted by December 2018 and prior to first disbursement. (2016 Baseline: no ESMS) Progress/Status: The ESMS was established in December 2018.The updated ESMS document have been approved by the PPP Policy & Monitoring Board in January 2023.
Data Source: PPPPA Reports; ADB Review Mission reports. Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y

Output: PPP institutional capacity enhanced and strengthened. Indicator: VGF Guidelines approved by Steering Committee and adopted and made operational by July 2019. (2016 Baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: The updated VGF guidelines have been approved by the PPP Policy & Monitoring Board in January 2023.
Data Source: PPPPA reports; relevant Government of Punjab notification; ADB review Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2019 Target value: Y
Viable PPP projects that offer value-for-money increased.

By 2023: Private investment through PPPs for the provision of provincial infrastructure and service projects increased to 4% of the annual development program (2015-2016 Baseline: expenditure in PPP projects as a percentage of total development expenditure - 1.98%*) (The actual total expenditure and PPP sector expenditure was considerably lower than budgeted in annual development program (FY2016), hence actual expenditures are used as baseline for accuracy of data.) Progress/Status: Loan closed on 30 June 2025. Smart Water meters~ $7 million: Contract was awarded but due to dispute on ESCROW account profit sharing between private party and WASA. Progress was staled and now WASA has terminated the contract. ADB is following up with EA for refund of advance funds under the loan.
Multan-Vehari Road ~$50 million: Bidding was carried out and single bid was received but due to cost escalation government decided to re-tender but however at later stage government decided to move this from PPP mode to conventional procurement using government funds. Data Source: a. Finance Department reports; PPPPA status reports; PPP projects awarded as disclosed in P&DD website Actual value:
